criteria.text: The memo identifies that the Bill of Sale (Section 6) selects Arizona law and Maricopa County courts. It notes this conflicts with the APA's Delaware governing law (Section 10.10) and Delaware Court of Chancery forum (Section 10.11). It explains that because APA Section 10.13 makes the Bill of Sale control on transfer of title, title disputes could be split off to Arizona while other disputes stay in Delaware, exposing Buyer to parallel or inconsistent proceedings.
hints: Bill of Sale controls on transfer of title

criteria.text: The memo identifies that APA Section 8.5(b) excludes Buyer's indemnity for Assumed Liabilities from the Cap. It explains that, because Section 2.3(c) and Disclosure Schedule 2.3(c) make Seller's pre-closing workmanship/roof-penetration warranty obligations and/or the pending roof-leak class action Assumed Liabilities, Buyer bears uncapped exposure for Seller's pre-closing liabilities.

The memo identifies that APA Section 10.6 lets Seller assign its rights, including Earnout Payments and/or indemnity claims, without Buyer's consent. It explains that the assignee would get the Section 2.6(d) earnout information/audit rights over Buyer's confidential data (such as pipeline, pricing or books), so a competitor could become the assignee.

The memo identifies that Key Employee Agreement Section 9.2 requires Okafor-Lindqvist's prior written consent to assign the agreement, including on a sale of substantially all assets, and that assignment without consent is void. It also states that this consent is not listed on Disclosure Schedule 4.6 or made a closing condition under APA Section 7.2, so the assignment of the agreement (and its non-compete) to Buyer may be ineffective.
The memo states that the APA indemnification cap is 15% of the Base Purchase Price, or $2,760,000, on an $18,400,000 base price.
The memo states that the Key Employee Agreement contains a 24-month post-termination non-compete that Buyer stands to lose or fail to acquire.
The memo is addressed to the supervising partner. For each issue it identifies, it gives the document and section, why the issue matters to Roumoux, and a recommended fix.
The memo presents the issues in an explicit order of significance and includes proposed drafting language for at least one fix.
The memo does not conclude that APA Section 10.13's order-of-precedence clause resolves the governing law conflict in favor of Delaware for all disputes, including title disputes.
hints: Bill of Sale controls on transfer of title

criteria.text: The memo does not state that the employee's consent to assignment was obtained, or that it is listed on Disclosure Schedule 4.6 or required as a closing condition.
